haiku-low.q1: The scheduler starts attempt 1 at 02:00 UTC. It extracts replica orders rows with updated_at later than lo, where lo is H_old minus 2 hours (no lower bound on first run).
haiku-low.q2: A bulk-import row becomes visible only when its transaction commits, which can be up to 90 minutes after its updated_at.
haiku-low.q3: The edit has a newer updated_at, so a later nightly extract reads it and the MERGE updates the existing row, since the incoming updated_at is newer.
haiku-low.q4: The app's delete arrives as an update. The MERGE sets is_deleted to true and copies deleted_at. The job never removes the row from orders.
haiku-low.q5: The warehouse transaction rolls back, a failed row is logged, H stays unchanged, and the lease is released. Retry after 15 minutes, max three attempts; then page on-call.
haiku-low.q6: Dashboards show the last fully committed night, never a partial one. The 06:00 staleness check posts an alert to the data-alerts channel.
haiku-low.q7: The weekly Sunday reconciliation. It compares count and checksum for that creation day, and reloads the day from the replica if it differs.
haiku-low.q8: MERGE updates a row only when the incoming updated_at is strictly newer. Staging is reduced to one row per order_id with the greatest updated_at.
haiku-low.q9: Stored in etl_state. It holds H_new, the replica clock reading when the extract's snapshot opens. It is written in the same transaction as the MERGE, on success.
haiku-low.q10: The MERGE and the high-water mark update commit in one warehouse transaction, and orders changes only inside committed transactions. Dashboards read only committed rows.
haiku-low.q11: The retry deletes its own run_id's staged rows before inserting, replacing them. H_old is unchanged, so the retry extracts the same window, recomputed from H_old minus 2 hours.
haiku-low.q12: It re-reads that one creation day's rows from the replica, stages them, and MERGEs them into orders in its own transaction. It does not touch the high-water mark.

sonnet.q1: The scheduler starts attempt 1 at 02:00 UTC. It extracts replica `orders` rows with `updated_at` later than lo = H_old minus 2 hours (first ever run: no lower bound, all rows).
sonnet.q2: A bulk-import row becomes visible only when its transaction commits, which can be up to 90 minutes after its `updated_at`.
sonnet.q3: The edit raises the row's `updated_at`, so a later nightly extract reads it (window after lo). It is staged and MERGEd, updating the existing order_id row because the incoming updated_at is strictly newer.
sonnet.q4: The delete arrives as an update (deleted_at set). The MERGE updates the row, copies deleted_at, and sets is_deleted = true. The job never removes the row from `orders`.
sonnet.q5: The warehouse transaction is rolled back, a failed row is logged in etl_run_log, high_water_mark stays unchanged, and the lease is released. If fewer than 3 attempts have run, the next attempt starts 15 minutes after the failed one ends, going through lease check and window calculation again. After the third failure, on-call is paged.
sonnet.q6: Dashboards show the last fully committed night (never a partial night). The 06:00 staleness check finds no committed success for tonight in etl_state and posts an alert to the data-alerts channel.
sonnet.q7: The Sunday reconciliation, if that night's load committed. It compares count and checksum per creation day over the last 30 days (by created_at). It finds the mismatched day and reloads it from the replica via staging and MERGE.
sonnet.q8: Staging is reduced to one row per order_id (greatest updated_at), and the MERGE updates an existing row only if the incoming updated_at is strictly newer. An equal updated_at leaves the row alone, and an older one cannot overwrite a newer one.
sonnet.q9: In `etl_state` in the warehouse. The value is H_new, the replica's clock reading taken when the extract's snapshot opens (not the max updated_at seen). It is written inside the same warehouse transaction as the MERGE, committed together with the data.
sonnet.q10: `orders` changes only inside committed transactions, and the MERGE and high-water mark commit together in one transaction. Dashboards read only committed rows and never read staging.
sonnet.q11: The retry first deletes any staging rows carrying its own run_id, so it replaces the earlier staging instead of adding to it. Since H is unchanged after failure, the retry recalculates the same window: lo = H_old minus 2 hours.
sonnet.q12: It re-reads from the replica the rows of that one creation day (by created_at). It copies them into staging and MERGEs into `orders` in its own transaction, using the same merge rules. It does not touch the high-water mark H.
